+#!/bin/bash
+# Checks that the review workflows fire the cloud routine and never use the desktop runner.
+# Runs scripts/start_review.sh against a local mock of the routine endpoint.
+set -uo pipefail
+repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'kill "$server_pid" 2>/dev/null; find "$work" -delete' EXIT
+failures=0
+
+fail() { echo "FAIL: $*"; failures=$((failures + 1)); }
+pass() { echo "ok: $*"; }
+
+# A stub reviewer CLI on PATH. If the script calls it, the test fails.
+mkdir "$work/bin"
+printf '#!/bin/bash\ntouch %q/reviewer-called\n' "$work" > "$work/bin/reviewer"
+chmod +x "$work/bin/reviewer"
+
+cat > "$work/server.py" <<'EOF'
+import http.server, json, sys
+work = sys.argv[1]
+class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"]))
+        with open(f"{work}/request.json", "w") as f:
+            json.dump({"path": self.path,
+                       "auth": self.headers.get("Authorization"),
+                       "body": json.loads(body)}, f)
+        status = int(self.path.rsplit("/", 1)[1])
+        self.send_response(status)
+        self.end_headers()
+        self.wfile.write(b"routine output\n")
+    def log_message(self, *a): pass
+server = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
+print(server.server_port, flush=True)
+server.serve_forever()
+EOF
+coproc SERVER { python3 -I "$work/server.py" "$work"; }
+server_pid=$SERVER_PID
+read -r port <&"${SERVER[0]}"
+
+run_with_status() {
+  rm -f "$work/request.json" "$work/reviewer-called"
+  PATH="$work/bin:$PATH" \
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$port/routine/$1" \
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=test-token \
+  REVIEW_MODEL=test-model \
+  REVIEW_EFFORT=high \
+    bash "$repo/scripts/start_review.sh" 42 >/dev/null 2>&1
+}
+
+run_with_status 200; code=$?
+[ "$code" -eq 0 ] && pass "200 exits 0" || fail "200 exited $code"
+[ ! -e "$work/reviewer-called" ] && pass "local reviewer CLI not called" || fail "local reviewer CLI was called"
+if [ -e "$work/request.json" ]; then
+  jq -e '.auth == "Bearer test-token"' "$work/request.json" >/dev/null && pass "bearer token sent" || fail "bearer token missing"
+  jq -e '.body == {pull_request: 42, model: "test-model", effort: "high"}' "$work/request.json" >/dev/null \
+    && pass "JSON body carries pull_request, model, effort" || fail "JSON body wrong: $(jq -c .body "$work/request.json")"
+else
+  fail "routine was not called"
+fi
+
+run_with_status 422; code=$?
+[ "$code" -ne 0 ] && pass "422 exits non-zero" || fail "422 exited 0"
+
+run_with_status 500; code=$?
+[ "$code" -ne 0 ] && pass "500 exits non-zero" || fail "500 exited 0"
+
+if grep -n 'desktop' "$repo"/.github/workflows/*.yml; then
+  fail "a workflow still targets the desktop runner"
+else
+  pass "no workflow targets the desktop runner"
+fi
+
+[ "$failures" -eq 0 ] && echo "PASS" || { echo "$failures failure(s)"; exit 1; }

 #!/bin/bash
+# Fires the cloud routine that runs the reviewer (see docs/cloud-routine.md).
+# Exits 0 when the review passed and non-zero otherwise.
 set -euo pipefail
 pull_request_number=$1
-reviewer exec review \
-  --model "${REVIEW_MODEL:?}" \
-  --effort "${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}" \
-  --pull-request "$pull_request_number" \
-  --post-comments
+model="${REVIEW_MODEL:?}"
+effort="${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}"
+url="${CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL:?}"
+token="${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}"
+
+if [[ ! "$pull_request_number" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
+  echo "pull request number must be an integer: $pull_request_number" >&2
+  exit 2
+fi
+for value in "$model" "$effort"; do
+  if [[ "$value" == *[\"\\[:cntrl:]]* ]]; then
+    echo "REVIEW_MODEL and REVIEW_EFFORT must not contain quotes, backslashes or control characters" >&2
+    exit 2
+  fi
+done
+

+trap 'unlink "$response"' EXIT
+

+#!/bin/bash
+# Checks that the review workflows stay off the desktop runner and that
+# scripts/start_review.sh fires the cloud routine and maps its status codes.
+set -euo pipefail
+root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'kill "$server_pid" 2>/dev/null || true; find "$work" -delete' EXIT
+failures=0
+fail() { echo "FAIL: $*"; failures=$((failures + 1)); }
+
+for workflow in "$root"/.github/workflows/*.yml; do
+  if grep -q 'desktop' "$workflow"; then fail "$(basename "$workflow") still targets the desktop runner"; fi
+  grep -q 'CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN }}' "$workflow" || fail "$(basename "$workflow") does not pass CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN"
+  grep -q 'CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL: ${{ vars.CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL }}' "$workflow" || fail "$(basename "$workflow") does not pass CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL"
+done
+
+# Mock routine: answers with the status in $work/status and records the request.
+cat > "$work/server.py" <<'EOF'
+import http.server, json, sys
+work = sys.argv[1]
+class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"]))
+        with open(f"{work}/request.json", "w") as f:
+            json.dump({"auth": self.headers["Authorization"], "body": json.loads(body)}, f)
+        self.send_response(int(open(f"{work}/status").read()))
+        self.end_headers()
+        self.wfile.write(b"routine output")
+    def log_message(self, *a): pass
+s = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), H)
+open(f"{work}/port", "w").write(str(s.server_port))
+s.serve_forever()
+EOF
+python3 "$work/server.py" "$work" &
+server_pid=$!
+for _ in $(seq 50); do [ -s "$work/port" ] && break; sleep 0.1; done
+
+run() {
+  echo "$1" > "$work/status"
+  REVIEW_MODEL=m1 REVIEW_EFFORT=high CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$(cat "$work/port")/fire" \
+    CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=tok PATH="$work/nobin:$PATH" bash "$root/scripts/start_review.sh" 42 >/dev/null 2>&1
+}
+# A fake reviewer CLI that fails, so a run that still calls it locally is caught.
+mkdir -p "$work/nobin"
+printf '#!/bin/sh\necho "reviewer must not run locally" >&2\nexit 99\n' > "$work/nobin/reviewer"
+chmod +x "$work/nobin/reviewer"
+
+if run 200; then :; else fail "HTTP 200 should exit 0"; fi
+expected='{"auth": "Bearer tok", "body": {"pull_request": 42, "model": "m1", "effort": "high"}}'
+[ "$(cat "$work/request.json" 2>/dev/null)" = "$expected" ] || fail "request was $(cat "$work/request.json" 2>/dev/null), expected $expected"
+if run 422; then fail "HTTP 422 should exit non-zero"; fi
+if run 500; then fail "HTTP 500 should exit non-zero"; fi
+
+if [ "$failures" -eq 0 ]; then echo "PASS"; else exit 1; fi

+#!/bin/bash
+# Checks that the review workflows stay off the desktop runner and that
+# scripts/start_review.sh fires the cloud routine and maps its status codes.
+set -uo pipefail
+repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'kill "$server_pid" 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
+failures=0
+
+check() {
+  if [ "$2" = "$3" ]; then echo "ok   $1"; else echo "FAIL $1: expected '$2', got '$3'"; failures=$((failures + 1)); fi
+}
+
+# Workflows: no job on the desktop runner, and the start step gets the routine settings.
+for wf in pr-review rerun-review; do
+  file="$repo/.github/workflows/$wf.yml"
+  check "$wf has no desktop runner" 0 "$(grep -c 'desktop' "$file")"
+  check "$wf passes CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL" 1 "$(grep -c 'CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL: \${{ vars.CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL }}' "$file")"
+  check "$wf passes CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN" 1 "$(grep -c 'CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN: \${{ secrets.CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN }}' "$file")"
+  check "$wf still opens the check run" 1 "$(grep -c 'scripts/check_run.sh open' "$file")"
+  check "$wf still completes the check run" 1 "$(grep -c 'scripts/check_run.sh complete' "$file")"
+done
+
+# Stub routine: answers with the status in $work/status and records each request.
+cat > "$work/server.py" <<'EOF'
+import http.server, json, sys
+work = sys.argv[1]
+class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"]))
+        with open(f"{work}/request.json", "w") as f:
+            json.dump({"auth": self.headers.get("Authorization"), "body": json.loads(body)}, f)
+        self.send_response(int(open(f"{work}/status").read()))
+        self.end_headers()
+    def log_message(self, *a):
+        pass
+s = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), H)
+open(f"{work}/port", "w").write(str(s.server_port))
+s.serve_forever()
+EOF
+python3 "$work/server.py" "$work" &
+server_pid=$!
+for _ in $(seq 50); do [ -s "$work/port" ] && break; sleep 0.1; done
+
+run_with_status() {
+  echo "$1" > "$work/status"
+  rm -f "$work/request.json"
+  PATH="/usr/bin:/bin" \
+    CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$(cat "$work/port")/fire" \
+    CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=test-token REVIEW_MODEL=test-model REVIEW_EFFORT=high \
+    bash "$repo/scripts/start_review.sh" 42 >/dev/null 2>&1
+  echo $?
+}
+
+check "200 passes" 0 "$(run_with_status 200)"
+check "request body" '{"effort":"high","model":"test-model","pull_request":42}' \
+  "$(jq -cS .body "$work/request.json" 2>/dev/null)"
+check "bearer token" "Bearer test-token" "$(jq -r .auth "$work/request.json" 2>/dev/null)"
+check "422 fails" 1 "$(run_with_status 422)"
+check "500 fails" 1 "$(run_with_status 500)"
+check "non-numeric pull request fails" 1 "$(PATH=/usr/bin:/bin CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:1/ \
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=t REVIEW_MODEL=m REVIEW_EFFORT=e bash "$repo/scripts/start_review.sh" '1;x' >/dev/null 2>&1; echo $?)"
+# Port 1 on loopback refuses the connection, which is a transport error.
+check "transport error fails" 1 "$(PATH=/usr/bin:/bin CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:1/ \
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=t REVIEW_MODEL=m REVIEW_EFFORT=e bash "$repo/scripts/start_review.sh" 42 >/dev/null 2>&1; echo $?)"
+check "token stays off the curl command line" 0 "$(grep -c 'Bearer.*\$CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN\|-H.*Authorization\|--header.*Authorization' "$repo/scripts/start_review.sh")"
+
+# The workflows run the scripts directly, so git must track them as executable.
+for script in check_run.sh start_review.sh; do
+  check "$script is executable in git" 100755 "$(git -C "$repo" ls-files -s "scripts/$script" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
+done
+
+echo "$failures failure(s)"
+[ "$failures" -eq 0 ]

+#!/bin/bash
+# Runs start_review.sh against a local fake routine and checks that no workflow uses the desktop runner.
+set -uo pipefail
+root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'kill "$server" 2>/dev/null; find "$work" -delete' EXIT
+
+cat > "$work/server.py" <<'EOF'
+import http.server, json, sys
+class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"])))
+        with open(sys.argv[2], "w") as f:
+            json.dump({"auth": self.headers["Authorization"], "body": body}, f)
+        self.send_response(int(self.path.strip("/")))
+        self.end_headers()
+    def log_message(self, *a): pass
+s = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), H)
+open(sys.argv[1], "w").write(str(s.server_port))
+s.serve_forever()
+EOF
+python3 "$work/server.py" "$work/port" "$work/request" &
+server=$!
+for _ in $(seq 50); do [ -s "$work/port" ] && break; sleep 0.1; done
+port=$(cat "$work/port")
+
+failures=0
+check() {
+  local name=$1 want=$2 got=$3
+  if [ "$want" = "$got" ]; then echo "PASS $name"; else echo "FAIL $name: want $want, got $got"; failures=$((failures + 1)); fi
+}
+run() {
+  REVIEW_MODEL=m1 REVIEW_EFFORT=high CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=tok \
+    CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$port/$1" "$root/scripts/start_review.sh" 42 >/dev/null 2>&1
+  echo $?
+}
+
+check "200 passes" 0 "$(run 200)"
+check "request body" '{"pull_request": 42, "model": "m1", "effort": "high"}' \
+  "$(python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.dumps(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["body"]))' "$work/request")"
+check "bearer token" "Bearer tok" \
+  "$(python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["auth"])' "$work/request")"
+REVIEW_MODEL='a"b\c' REVIEW_EFFORT=high CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=tok \
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$port/200" "$root/scripts/start_review.sh" 42 >/dev/null 2>&1
+check "quotes in model" 'a"b\c' \
+  "$(python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["body"]["model"])' "$work/request")"
+: > "$work/request"
+REVIEW_MODEL=m1 REVIEW_EFFORT=high CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$port/200" \
+  "$root/scripts/start_review.sh" 42 >/dev/null 2>&1
+check "missing token fails without a request" "1 0" "$? $(wc -c < "$work/request")"
+check "422 fails" 1 "$(run 422)"
+check "500 fails" 1 "$(run 500)"
+check "no desktop runner" 0 "$(grep -l desktop "$root"/.github/workflows/*.yml | wc -l)"
+
+exit "$failures"

+#!/bin/bash
+# Checks that every review goes through the cloud routine (docs/cloud-routine.md)
+# and that no review workflow can run on the desktop runner.
+# Run from anywhere: tests/cloud_review_test.sh
+set -uo pipefail
+repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+stub_pid=
+stop_stub() { [ -n "$stub_pid" ] && kill "$stub_pid" 2>/dev/null && wait "$stub_pid" 2>/dev/null; stub_pid=; }
+trap 'stop_stub; find "$work" -delete' EXIT
+failures=0
+
+fail() { echo "FAIL: $*"; failures=$((failures + 1)); }
+pass() { echo "ok:   $*"; }
+
+# Starts the stub routine answering with status $1; sets stub_pid and port.
+start_stub() {
+  stop_stub
+  : >"$work/request.json"
+  STUB_STATUS=$1 STUB_LOG="$work/request.json" python3 "$repo/tests/stub_routine.py" >"$work/port" &
+  stub_pid=$!
+  for _ in $(seq 50); do [ -s "$work/port" ] && break; sleep 0.1; done
+  port=$(cat "$work/port")
+}
+
+# Runs start_review.sh for pull request 42 against the stub; prints its exit code.
+run_review() {
+  (
+    cd "$work" || exit 99
+    PATH="$work/no-reviewer:$PATH" \
+      CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$port/fire" \
+      CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=test-token \
+      REVIEW_MODEL=test-model REVIEW_EFFORT=high \
+      "$repo/scripts/start_review.sh" 42 >"$work/out" 2>&1
+  )
+  echo $?
+}
+
+# A `reviewer` on PATH that records any local run, so a desktop-style fallback shows up.
+mkdir -p "$work/no-reviewer"
+printf '#!/bin/bash\ntouch "%s/reviewer-ran"\n' "$work" >"$work/no-reviewer/reviewer"
+chmod +x "$work/no-reviewer/reviewer"
+
+# 1. Review passed: 200 -> exit 0, correct request.
+start_stub 200
+code=$(run_review)
+[ "$code" = 0 ] && pass "200 exits 0" || fail "200 should exit 0, got $code: $(cat "$work/out")"
+if [ -s "$work/request.json" ]; then
+  python3 - "$work/request.json" <<'EOF' && pass "request carries token and body" || fail "request is wrong: $(cat "$work/request.json")"
+import json, sys
+r = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
+body = json.loads(r["body"])
+assert r["path"] == "/fire", r
+assert r["authorization"] == "Bearer test-token", r
+assert r["content_type"] == "application/json", r
+assert body == {"pull_request": 42, "model": "test-model", "effort": "high"}, body
+EOF
+else
+  fail "no request reached the cloud routine"
+fi
+
+# 2. Blocking findings: 422 -> exit 1, so the check run fails.
+start_stub 422
+code=$(run_review)
+[ "$code" = 1 ] && pass "422 exits 1" || fail "422 should exit 1, got $code"
+
+# 3. Routine failure: 500 -> exit 2, and no local reviewer fallback.
+start_stub 500
+code=$(run_review)
+[ "$code" = 2 ] && pass "500 exits 2" || fail "500 should exit 2, got $code"
+
+# 4. Routine unreachable -> exit 2, and no local reviewer fallback.
+stop_stub
+code=$(run_review)
+[ "$code" = 2 ] && pass "unreachable routine exits 2" || fail "unreachable routine should exit 2, got $code"
+
+[ -e "$work/reviewer-ran" ] && fail "the reviewer CLI ran locally" || pass "the reviewer CLI never ran locally"
+
+# 5. Workflows: no desktop runner, same triggers, cloud settings passed in.
+for wf in pr-review rerun-review; do
+  file="$repo/.github/workflows/$wf.yml"
+  grep -q 'desktop' "$file" && fail "$wf.yml still names the desktop runner" || pass "$wf.yml has no desktop runner"
+  grep -q 'self-hosted' "$file" && fail "$wf.yml still uses a self-hosted runner" || pass "$wf.yml has no self-hosted runner"
+  grep -q 'runs-on: ubuntu-latest' "$file" && pass "$wf.yml runs on a GitHub-hosted runner" || fail "$wf.yml does not run on ubuntu-latest"
+  grep -q 'CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL: ${{ vars.CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL }}' "$file" &&
+    grep -q 'CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN }}' "$file" &&
+    pass "$wf.yml passes the cloud routine settings" || fail "$wf.yml does not pass the cloud routine settings"
+  grep -B1 'run: scripts/check_run.sh complete' "$file" | grep -q 'if: always()' && pass "$wf.yml still completes the ai-review check" || fail "$wf.yml no longer completes the ai-review check"
+done
+grep -q 'types: \[opened, synchronize\]' "$repo/.github/workflows/pr-review.yml" && pass "pr-review trigger unchanged" || fail "pr-review trigger changed"
+grep -q "startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/rereview')" "$repo/.github/workflows/rerun-review.yml" && pass "rerun-review trigger unchanged" || fail "rerun-review trigger changed"
+
+echo
+[ "$failures" = 0 ] && echo "PASS" || { echo "$failures check(s) failed"; exit 1; }

+"""Stub of the cloud review routine for tests/cloud_review_test.sh.
+
+Answers every POST with the status in STUB_STATUS and records the request
+headers and body as JSON in the file named by STUB_LOG.
+"""
+import json
+import os
+import sys
+from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer
+
+
+class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
+        body = self.rfile.read(length).decode()
+        with open(os.environ["STUB_LOG"], "w") as log:
+            json.dump(
+                {
+                    "path": self.path,
+                    "authorization": self.headers.get("Authorization"),
+                    "content_type": self.headers.get("Content-Type"),
+                    "body": body,
+                },
+                log,
+            )
+        self.send_response(int(os.environ["STUB_STATUS"]))
+        self.end_headers()
+        self.wfile.write(b'{"message": "stub"}')
+
+    def log_message(self, *args):
+        pass
+
+
+server = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
+print(server.server_port, flush=True)
+sys.stdout.close()
+server.serve_forever()

+#!/bin/bash
+# Checks that every review goes through the cloud routine with no desktop fallback.
+# Run from the repository root: tests/cloud_review_test.sh
+set -uo pipefail
+root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'find "$work" -delete' EXIT
+failures=0
+
+fail() { echo "FAIL: $*"; failures=$((failures + 1)); }
+pass() { echo "ok: $*"; }
+
+# Stubs: curl answers with $STUB_STATUS (or fails with $STUB_CURL_EXIT); reviewer records any call.
+mkdir -p "$work/bin"
+cat > "$work/bin/curl" <<'EOF'
+#!/bin/bash
+printf '%s\n' "$@" > "$STUB_DIR/curl_args"
+if [ -n "${STUB_CURL_EXIT:-}" ]; then exit "$STUB_CURL_EXIT"; fi
+printf '%s' "$STUB_STATUS"
+EOF
+cat > "$work/bin/reviewer" <<'EOF'
+#!/bin/bash
+echo called >> "$STUB_DIR/reviewer_called"
+EOF
+chmod +x "$work/bin/curl" "$work/bin/reviewer"
+
+run_case() {
+  local name=$1 expected=$2 status=$3 curl_exit=$4
+  : > "$work/curl_args"
+  : > "$work/reviewer_called"
+  PATH="$work/bin:$PATH" STUB_DIR="$work" STUB_STATUS="$status" STUB_CURL_EXIT="$curl_exit" \
+    CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL=https://routine.example/fire CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=tok123 \
+    REVIEW_MODEL=m1 REVIEW_EFFORT=high \
+    bash "$root/scripts/start_review.sh" 42 > /dev/null 2>&1
+  local got=$?
+  if [ "$got" = "$expected" ]; then pass "$name exits $expected"; else fail "$name exits $got, want $expected"; fi
+  if [ -s "$work/reviewer_called" ]; then fail "$name ran the local reviewer CLI"; else pass "$name did not run the local reviewer"; fi
+}
+
+run_case "status 200" 0 200 ""
+run_case "status 422" 1 422 ""
+run_case "status 500" 2 500 ""
+run_case "curl timeout" 2 "" 28
+
+# The request goes to the routine with the token and the documented body.
+run_case "request shape" 0 200 "" > /dev/null
+args=$(cat "$work/curl_args")
+grep -qx 'https://routine.example/fire' <<< "$args" && pass "request uses CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL" || fail "request does not use CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL"
+grep -qx 'Authorization: Bearer tok123' <<< "$args" && pass "request sends the bearer token" || fail "request does not send the bearer token"
+body=$(grep -x '{.*}' <<< "$args" | head -n 1)
+if [ "$(jq -c . <<< "$body" 2> /dev/null)" = '{"pull_request":42,"model":"m1","effort":"high"}' ]; then
+  pass "request body carries pull_request, model, effort"
+else
+  fail "request body is '$body'"
+fi
+grep -q -- '--retry' <<< "$args" && fail "request retries" || pass "request does not retry"
+
+# The workflows call the scripts directly, so they must be executable.
+for script in check_run.sh start_review.sh; do
+  [ -x "$root/scripts/$script" ] && pass "$script is executable" || fail "$script is not executable"
+done
+
+# No workflow names a self-hosted runner anywhere, and each job's timeout covers the routine wait.
+max_time=$(grep -oE -- '--max-time [0-9]+' "$root/scripts/start_review.sh" | grep -oE '[0-9]+')
+for wf in "$root"/.github/workflows/*.yml; do
+  name=$(basename "$wf")
+  if grep -Eq 'self-hosted|desktop' "$wf"; then fail "$name names a self-hosted runner"; else pass "$name names no self-hosted runner"; fi
+  timeout=$(grep -oE 'timeout-minutes: [0-9]+' "$wf" | grep -oE '[0-9]+')
+  if [ -n "$timeout" ] && [ -n "$max_time" ] && [ $((timeout * 60)) -gt "$max_time" ]; then
+    pass "$name timeout covers the routine wait"
+  else
+    fail "$name timeout '$timeout' min does not cover --max-time '$max_time' s"
+  fi
+done
+
+# Triggers match today's events exactly: everything above "jobs:", plus the /rereview filter.
+header() { sed '/^jobs:/q' "$1"; }
+expected_pr=$'name: pr-review\non:\n  pull_request:\n    types: [opened, synchronize]\n\njobs:'
+expected_rerun=$'name: rerun-review\non:\n  issue_comment:\n    types: [created]\n\njobs:'
+expected_if="    if: github.event.issue.pull_request && startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/rereview')"
+[ "$(header "$root/.github/workflows/pr-review.yml")" = "$expected_pr" ] \
+  && pass "pr-review triggers unchanged" || fail "pr-review triggers changed"
+[ "$(header "$root/.github/workflows/rerun-review.yml")" = "$expected_rerun" ] \
+  && pass "rerun-review triggers unchanged" || fail "rerun-review triggers changed"
+grep -qxF "$expected_if" "$root/.github/workflows/rerun-review.yml" \
+  && pass "rerun-review /rereview filter unchanged" || fail "rerun-review /rereview filter changed"
+
+# The ai-review check is opened and completed from the workflow, with the job's real status.
+check_wiring() {
+  local wf=$1 open_line=$2 complete_line=$3
+  local name
+  name=$(basename "$wf")
+  grep -qxF "        run: $open_line" "$wf" && pass "$name opens the check run" || fail "$name does not open the check run"
+  grep -qxF "        run: $complete_line" "$wf" && pass "$name completes the check with job.status" || fail "$name does not complete the check with job.status"
+  grep -A1 'name: Complete check run' "$wf" | grep -qxF '        if: always()' \
+    && pass "$name always completes the check" || fail "$name does not always complete the check"
+}
+
+# The review step runs the cloud script with the routine settings, and its failure fails the job.
+review_step() {
+  local wf=$1 number=$2
+  local name expected
+  name=$(basename "$wf")
+  expected="      - name: Start reviewer
+        run: scripts/start_review.sh \"\${{ $number }}\"
+        env:
+          REVIEW_MODEL: \${{ vars.REVIEW_MODEL }}
+          REVIEW_EFFORT: \${{ vars.REVIEW_EFFORT }}
+          CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL: \${{ vars.CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL }}
+          CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN: \${{ secrets.CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN }}
+      - name: Complete check run"
+  [ "$(sed -n '/- name: Start reviewer/,/- name: Complete check run/p' "$wf")" = "$expected" ] \
+    && pass "$name review step calls the cloud routine and can fail the job" \
+    || fail "$name review step changed"
+}
+review_step "$root/.github/workflows/pr-review.yml" 'github.event.pull_request.number'
+review_step "$root/.github/workflows/rerun-review.yml" 'github.event.issue.number'
+
+# A missing setting is a routine failure (exit 2), never a blocking-findings result (exit 1).
+PATH="$work/bin:$PATH" STUB_DIR="$work" STUB_STATUS=200 REVIEW_EFFORT=high \
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL=https://routine.example/fire CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=tok123 \
+  bash "$root/scripts/start_review.sh" 42 > /dev/null 2>&1
+got=$?
+[ "$got" = 2 ] && pass "missing REVIEW_MODEL exits 2" || fail "missing REVIEW_MODEL exits $got, want 2"
+
+check_wiring "$root/.github/workflows/pr-review.yml" \
+  'scripts/check_run.sh open "${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}"' \
+  'scripts/check_run.sh complete "${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}" "${{ job.status }}"'
+check_wiring "$root/.github/workflows/rerun-review.yml" \
+  'scripts/check_run.sh open-for-pr "${{ github.event.issue.number }}"' \
+  'scripts/check_run.sh complete-for-pr "${{ github.event.issue.number }}" "${{ job.status }}"'
+
+echo
+if [ "$failures" -eq 0 ]; then echo "PASS"; else echo "FAIL ($failures)"; exit 1; fi

+#!/bin/bash
+# Checks that every review goes through the cloud routine and never the desktop.
+set -uo pipefail
+repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+failures=0
+fail() { echo "FAIL: $*"; failures=$((failures + 1)); }
+pass() { echo "ok: $*"; }
+
+cat > "$work/mock.py" <<'EOF'
+import http.server, json, sys
+status, log = int(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2]
+class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"]))
+        with open(log, "a") as f:
+            f.write(json.dumps({"auth": self.headers["Authorization"], "body": json.loads(body)}) + "\n")
+        self.send_response(status); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(b"mock")
+    def log_message(self, *a): pass
+s = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), H)
+print(s.server_port, flush=True)
+s.serve_forever()
+EOF
+
+run_against() {
+  local status=$1 log="$work/log-$1"
+  : > "$log"
+  python3 -I "$work/mock.py" "$status" "$log" > "$work/port-$status" &
+  local pid=$!
+  for _ in $(seq 50); do [ -s "$work/port-$status" ] && break; sleep 0.1; done
+  local port
+  port=$(cat "$work/port-$status")
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$port/fire" CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=tok REVIEW_MODEL=m1 REVIEW_EFFORT=high \
+    "$repo/scripts/cloud_review.sh" 42 > /dev/null 2>&1
+  local code=$?
+  kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null; wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null
+  echo "$code"
+}
+
+script="$repo/scripts/cloud_review.sh"
+if [ ! -x "$script" ]; then
+  fail "scripts/cloud_review.sh is missing or not executable"
+else
+  [ "$(run_against 200)" = 0 ] && pass "HTTP 200 passes" || fail "HTTP 200 must exit 0"
+  [ "$(run_against 422)" != 0 ] && pass "HTTP 422 fails" || fail "HTTP 422 must exit non-zero"
+  [ "$(run_against 500)" != 0 ] && pass "HTTP 500 fails" || fail "HTTP 500 must exit non-zero"
+  expected='{"auth":"Bearer tok","body":{"effort":"high","model":"m1","pull_request":42}}'
+  got=$(jq -cS . "$work/log-200")
+  [ "$got" = "$expected" ] && pass "one request with the right body and token" || fail "request was: $got"
+  [ "$(wc -l < "$work/log-500")" = 1 ] && pass "no retry after a failure" || fail "expected one request after HTTP 500"
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:9/fire" CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=tok REVIEW_MODEL=m1 REVIEW_EFFORT=high \
+    "$script" 42 > /dev/null 2>&1 && fail "a connection error must exit non-zero" || pass "connection error fails"
+fi
+
+for wf in pr-review rerun-review; do
+  f="$repo/.github/workflows/$wf.yml"
+  grep -q 'desktop' "$f" && fail "$wf uses the desktop runner" || pass "$wf has no desktop runner"
+  grep -q 'start_review\|reviewer exec' "$f" && fail "$wf starts a local reviewer" || pass "$wf has no local reviewer"
+  grep -q 'scripts/cloud_review.sh' "$f" && pass "$wf calls the cloud routine" || fail "$wf does not call the cloud routine"
+  grep -q 'check_run.sh open' "$f" && grep -q 'check_run.sh complete' "$f" && pass "$wf keeps the ai-review check" || fail "$wf lost a check-run step"
+done
+grep -q 'types: \[opened, synchronize\]' "$repo/.github/workflows/pr-review.yml" && pass "pr-review trigger unchanged" || fail "pr-review trigger changed"
+grep -q "if: github.event.issue.pull_request && startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/rereview')" "$repo/.github/workflows/rerun-review.yml" \
+  && grep -q 'types: \[created\]' "$repo/.github/workflows/rerun-review.yml" && pass "rerun-review trigger unchanged" || fail "rerun-review trigger changed"
+for s in scripts/check_run.sh scripts/cloud_review.sh; do
+  git -C "$repo" ls-files -s "$s" | grep -q '^100755' && pass "$s is executable in git" || fail "$s is not executable in git"
+done
+[ -e "$repo/scripts/start_review.sh" ] && fail "the desktop script start_review.sh still exists" || pass "no desktop script"
+
+find "$work" -delete
+[ "$failures" = 0 ] && echo "PASS" || { echo "$failures failure(s)"; exit 1; }

+wfdir="$root/.github/workflows"

+for wf in "$wfdir"/*.yml; do

+    fail "$name names a self-hosted runner"
+  elif [ "$(grep -c '^\s*runs-on:' "$wf")" != "$(grep -c '^\s*runs-on: ubuntu-latest$' "$wf")" ]; then
+    fail "$name has a job off ubuntu-latest"
+  else
+    pass "$name runs on ubuntu-latest"
+  fi
+done

+# 2. Triggers are unchanged: the whole on: block and the rerun filter match today's.
+on_block() { sed -n '/^on:/,/^jobs:/p' "$1" | tr '\n' '|'; }

+  && pass "pr-review trigger unchanged" || fail "pr-review trigger changed"
+[ "$(on_block "$wfdir/rerun-review.yml")" = 'on:|  issue_comment:|    types: [created]||jobs:|' ] \
+  && grep -qx "    if: github.event.issue.pull_request && startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/rereview')" "$wfdir/rerun-review.yml" \
+  && pass "rerun-review trigger unchanged" || fail "rerun-review trigger changed"
+

+#!/bin/bash
+# Runs the review through the cloud routine (docs/cloud-routine.md).
+# Exits 0 when the review passed and 1 otherwise. There is no local fallback.
+set -euo pipefail
+pull_request_number=$1
+model=${REVIEW_MODEL:?}
+effort=${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}
+: "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL:?}" "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}"
+
+[[ $pull_request_number =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || { echo "pull request number must be an integer: $pull_request_number" >&2; exit 2; }
+safe='^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+$'
+[[ $model =~ $safe ]] || { echo "REVIEW_MODEL has characters outside $safe" >&2; exit 2; }
+[[ $effort =~ $safe ]] || { echo "REVIEW_EFFORT has characters outside $safe" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+body=$(printf '{"pull_request":%s,"model":"%s","effort":"%s"}' "$pull_request_number" "$model" "$effort")
+token=${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN//\\/\\\\}
+token=${token//\"/\\\"}
+
+# The routine waits up to 30 minutes. The token goes in on stdin to keep it out of argv.
+status=$(printf 'header = "Authorization: Bearer %s"\n' "$token" | curl --config - \
+  --silent --show-error --max-time 1860 \
+  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+  --data "$body" \
+  --output /dev/null --write-out '%{http_code}' \
+  "$CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL") || { echo "cloud routine request failed" >&2; exit 1; }
+
+case "$status" in
+  200) echo "cloud review passed" ;;
+  422) echo "cloud review reported blocking findings" >&2; exit 1 ;;
+  *) echo "cloud routine failed with HTTP $status" >&2; exit 1 ;;
+esac

# Plan: run PR reviews on the cloud routine

I read every file in the repository. A separate verifier agent then checked my findings and an earlier draft of this plan. It confirmed all seven findings and found gaps in five plan pieces. The plan below includes its fixes. It could not check GitHub's documentation live this session. So the points about GitHub's concurrency and cancel behaviour come from what we know of the docs, not from a live check.

## What the files show

- Both workflows run on `[self-hosted, desktop]` and start the reviewer CLI there (`.github/workflows/pr-review.yml:8`, `.github/workflows/rerun-review.yml:9`, `scripts/start_review.sh:4`).
- The NAS can do short jobs and HTTP calls. It cannot run the reviewer CLI (`README.md:23`).
- The routine runs the review and posts the comments itself. The POST waits up to 30 minutes. It returns 200 for a pass and 422 for blocking findings. Any other status means the routine failed (`docs/cloud-routine.md:5-7`).
- The cloud proxy refuses writes to the check-runs API (`notes/findings.md:3`). So the `ai-review` check run has to stay in GitHub Actions.
- Merges need `ai-review` to pass (`notes/findings.md:5`). A missing or stuck check blocks merges.
- All reviews share one reviewer sign-in. Two refreshes at the same moment can sign one session out (`notes/findings.md:2`). The docs do not say who refreshes the sign-in, or whether the routine runs reviews one at a time.
- The App key has only ever been used from the desktop (`notes/findings.md:4`).
- There is a bug today: `complete` creates a second check run and leaves the first one in progress (`scripts/check_run.sh:9-12`). `complete-for-pr` also reads the PR's head commit at the end of the run. After a 30-minute wait, that commit can be newer than the one the review checked.

## Steps

1. **Add the eval first.** Write a test that runs a new `scripts/fire_routine.sh` against a local stub server. The stub returns 200, 422 and 500, and one case never answers. The test checks the exit code for each case, the bearer header, and the JSON body. A test variable sets a short timeout. It must fail before the script exists. # Plan: move PR reviews from the desktop to the cloud routine

A fresh verifier agent checked the research and a first draft of this plan. I revised the plan to fix the gaps it found. The repo has no remote, so nobody has checked the live secrets, branch protection, or the NAS.

## What the repo says

- Both workflows run on `[self-hosted, desktop]`. Each one runs `scripts/start_review.sh`, and that script starts the reviewer CLI (`.github/workflows/pr-review.yml:8`, `scripts/start_review.sh:4`).
- You start the cloud routine with a POST to `CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL`, using the bearer secret `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN`. The routine posts the review comments itself. The request can take up to 30 minutes. A `200` means the review passed, a `422` means blocking findings, and any other status means the routine failed (`docs/cloud-routine.md`).
- The cloud session's proxy refuses check-run writes, and branch protection requires `ai-review` (`notes/findings.md` #3, #5). So the GitHub Actions job must still open and complete the check run itself.
- The NAS runner can make HTTP calls but cannot run the reviewer CLI (`README.md:23`). After this change the runner only makes an HTTP call, so the NAS can host the job.

## Decision needed from you first

**Where the check-run token comes from.** This decision blocks step 2.
- **Option A:** mint the review App token on the NAS. The App key has only ever been used from the desktop (findings #4), so this would be the key's first use anywhere else.
- **Option B:** use `GITHUB_TOKEN` with `checks: write`. Check runs made this way show up as the `github-actions` app. If branch protection requires `ai-review` to come from the review App, the check will never pass.

## Steps

1. **Eval first.** Add `scripts/test_fire_routine.sh`. It starts a local stub server and runs the new script against four replies: `200`, `422`, `500`, and a hang. The test lowers the timeout so the hang case finishes fast. It must fail before step 2 exists, pass after it, and fail again when step 2 is undone.
2. **Add `scripts/fire_routine.sh`.** It sends a POST with the JSON body `{pull_request, model, effort}` and a `--max-time` a little over 30 minutes. A `200` exits with 0. A `422` exits with 1 and prints "blocking findings". Any other status, a curl transport error, or a `000` exits with 1 and prints "routine failed: <status>".
3. **Edit both workflows.**
   - Set `runs-on: [self-hosted, nas]` and `timeout-minutes: 35`.
   - Keep the token, open-check, and complete-check steps, with the token source you choose above.
   - Replace the `start_review.sh` step with `fire_routine.sh`. Pass it `vars.CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL`, `secrets.CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN`, `vars.REVIEW_MODEL`, and `vars.REVIEW_EFFORT`.
4. **Check the NAS before the cutover.** Confirm it has `gh`, `curl`, and `jq`. Confirm it can reach `CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` and can hold a connection open for 30 minutes.
5. **Cut over in one pull request.** For `pull_request` events, GitHub uses the workflow file from the PR branch. So the PR that changes `pr-review.yml` reviews itself on the new path. That run, plus a desktop run on the old state, is the proof for "Proof in practice". `/rereview` runs from the default branch, so test it right after the merge. Leave the desktop runner registered, so a revert restores the old path.
6. **Clean up.** Remove `scripts/start_review.sh` with `git rm`. Update the README text at lines 5–7 and 16, and update the Runners and Workflows tables.

Side by side, the old and new paths would post every review twice and double the reviewer cost. That is why step 5 switches over in one pull request.

## Effects to know about

- Each review holds the NAS runner for up to 30 minutes. The README calls the NAS a host for short jobs. If there is one NAS runner, reviews run one at a time, as they do on the desktop today.
- Fork PRs get no secrets, so their reviews fail on both the old path and the new one.

## New scope (I will ask before building any of these)

- **Sign-in refresh clash:** a guard so two sessions can't refresh the shared reviewer sign-in at the same moment and sign one out (findings #2). The refresh happens inside the cloud session, so the fix probably belongs there and not in this repo.

- **`/rereview` permissions:** anyone can comment `/rereview` (`rerun-review.yml:8`). Each rerun now costs cloud reviewer time.
- **Per-PR `concurrency` group:** it would stop two reviews of the same PR from running at once. Today's setup doesn't need it, so it is optional.

# Plan: move PR reviews from the desktop runner to the cloud routine

A fresh verifier agent checked my reading of the repo and a first draft of this plan. It confirmed six of the eight facts I based the plan on, said two were only partly right, and found gaps in four of the seven pieces. I fixed those gaps below. No verifier has checked this revised plan yet. I edited no files.

## Limits the plan has to fit

- **The check run has to stay in GitHub Actions.** The cloud network blocks writes to the GitHub check-runs API (`notes/findings.md`, finding 3). Branch protection needs `ai-review` to pass before merge (finding 5). So the workflows still create and finish the check, and the cloud routine only does the review.
- **The NAS can run the new job, with a cost.** It can make HTTP calls but cannot run the reviewer CLI (`README.md:23`). It is meant for short jobs, and each call to the routine waits up to 30 minutes for the review (`docs/cloud-routine.md:7`). So every review would tie up the NAS for up to 30 minutes.
- **The App key would be used from a new machine.** It has only ever been used from the desktop runner (finding 4). Any runner other than the desktop is a first.
- **Two reviews at once could break the shared sign-in.** It refreshes about every 10 days, and two sessions refreshing at once can sign one out (finding 2). Neither workflow has a `concurrency:` setting. Today, any one-at-a-time behaviour comes only from the desktop being a single runner.

## Questions for you before I build

1. Can the App key be used from the NAS? Or do you want a GitHub-hosted runner, which also keeps the NAS free?
2. Does the NAS have one runner or several? With several, reviews of different PRs can run at the same time and could break the shared sign-in. Running them one at a time would need a queue or lock, which is **new scope**. A plain GitHub `concurrency` group won't do it: it keeps only one waiting run and cancels the rest.
3. Do the `CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` variable and the `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN` secret exist? Does the desktop share the cloud's reviewer sign-in? The repo has no remote, so I couldn't check either.
4. Are `gh`, `curl` and `jq` installed on the NAS, and can it reach the routine URL?

## Pieces

1. **New `scripts/cloud_review.sh <pr>`** (in scope).
   - It sends a POST to `$CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` with the bearer token from the environment.
   - It builds the JSON body `{pull_request, model, effort}` with `jq`.
   - It reads the HTTP status with `-w '%{http_code}'` and sets `--max-time` a little over 1800 seconds.
   - It exits 0 on `200`. It exits 1 on `422` with the message "blocking findings". It exits 1 on any other status, including curl errors and timeouts (`000`), with the message "routine failed". It handles curl's own exit code so `set -e` can't skip that message.
2. **Both workflows** (in scope).
   - Change `runs-on` to the runner you pick in question 1.
   - Replace the "Start reviewer" step with `cloud_review.sh`. Pass `REVIEW_MODEL`, `REVIEW_EFFORT` and `CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` from repository variables, and `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN` from secrets.
   - Set `timeout-minutes: 40`.
   - Keep the App token, open-check, and `if: always()` finish-check steps as they are. A 40-minute job stays inside the App token's 1-hour lifetime (GitHub documentation).
   - A failed or timed-out job finishes the check as `failure` or `cancelled`, so merge stays blocked.
3. **README** (in scope). Update the text this change makes out of date: `README.md:5-7`, `:16` and `:22`.
4. **Keep `scripts/start_review.sh`** (in scope). Nothing will call it, but it keeps rollback to a simple revert. I can delete it in a later change if you want.
5. **Switch over in one change** (in scope). This stops the desktop and the cloud from refreshing the same sign-in at once, which matters only if they share one (question 3). It does not cover several cloud reviews at once (question 2). The desktop runner stays registered so we can roll back with a revert.
6. **Checks** (in scope).
   - A re-runnable local test of `cloud_review.sh` against a stub HTTP server that returns 200, 422 and 500, plus one call that times out. It fails before the script exists and passes after it.
   - Then a real test PR:
     - A clean PR gives `success`.
     - A PR with a known blocking finding gives `failure`.
     - A wrong token, set only in a test run (not the live secret), gives `failure`.
     - A timeout gives `cancelled`.
     - `/rereview` gives the same results.
   - For the "without" case, the desktop runner is offline and the check never finishes. Both runs get quoted in the PR.

## Rollout order

1. Merge to the default branch first. `/rereview` runs from the default branch, so it only works after the merge.
2. Run the checks in piece 6.
3. Take the desktop runner out of service once both workflows pass on the new runner.

Separate from this change: anyone who can comment on a PR can start a `/rereview`, and on the routine each one can run for up to 30 minutes.

# Plan: run PR reviews on the cloud routine

**Summary.** A GitHub runner keeps the `ai-review` check-run steps. The step that starts the reviewer becomes one HTTP POST to the cloud routine. The routine replies 200 when the review passes, 422 when it finds blocking issues, and any other code when the routine fails (`docs/cloud-routine.md:7`).

A fresh verifier agent checked the research and confirmed all 10 claims. A second verifier checked the first draft of this plan and found gaps in P1, P2, P5 and P7. The plan below includes those fixes. No verifier has checked this revised version yet.

## Facts that shape the plan
- **The check run cannot move.** The cloud session's proxy refuses writes to the check-runs API (`notes/findings.md:3`). The runner must open and complete `ai-review`.
- **The check gates merges.** Branch protection requires `ai-review` to pass (`notes/findings.md:5`). The check name must stay the same, and a routine failure must give a failing result.
- **The App key would be used somewhere new.** It has only ever been used from the desktop (`notes/findings.md:4`). Any new runner is a new host for it.
- **Parallel reviews have a sign-in risk.** Two reviews at once on one sign-in both finished with exit 0. If two sessions refresh the sign-in at the same moment, one can be signed out (`notes/findings.md:1-2`).

## Decisions for you
1. **Which runner?**
   - `ubuntu-latest` already has `gh`, `curl` and `jq`. It runs reviews in parallel, which brings back the sign-in refresh risk (see P8).
   - `[self-hosted, nas]`: the README calls it a runner for "short jobs" (`README.md:23`). Each review would hold it for up to 30 minutes.
2. **Can the review App's private key be used from that runner?**

## Pieces (in scope)
- **P1. New script `scripts/run_cloud_review.sh <pr>`.**
  - Require `${REVIEW_MODEL:?}` and `${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}`. Build the JSON body `{pull_request, model, effort}` with `jq`.
  - POST it to `$CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` with `Authorization: Bearer $CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN`.
  - Write the response body to a temp file with `-o`, print it to the log, then remove the file. Read the status with `-w '%{http_code}'`.
  - The timeout comes from `CLOUD_REVIEW_MAX_TIME`, default 1860 seconds. Catch curl's own exit code so that `set -e` does not stop the script before it reports the error.
  - Exit codes: 200 gives 0. 422 gives 1 with "blocking findings". Any other code, including `000`, gives 1 with "routine failed: HTTP <code>".
- **P2. Change both workflows.**
  - Set `runs-on` to the runner you choose and add `timeout-minutes: 35`.
  - Replace the "Start reviewer" step with the new script. Its env holds `REVIEW_MODEL`, `REVIEW_EFFORT`, `vars.CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` and `secrets.CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN`.
  - Leave the token, open and complete steps as they are. `job.status` still sets the conclusion.
- **P3. Remove the old script.** `git rm scripts/start_review.sh`. To roll back, revert the commit.
- **P4. Update the README.** Change the "Today the review runs on…desktop" paragraph, the sentence "Both workflows call `scripts/start_review.sh`", and the desktop row of the runner table.
- **P5. Test `tests/run_cloud_review_test.sh`.**
  - A local Python stub server answers with 200, 422 and 500, and also hangs (use a 2-second timeout override). A separate case uses a port with nothing listening.
  - Expected exit codes: 0, 1, 1, 1, 1.
  - The stub also checks the bearer header and the three JSON fields.
  - A wrong version of the script that maps 422 to 0 must fail the test. Undoing the fix must make the test fail again.
- **P6. Setup you need to do.**
  - Create the variable `CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` and the secret `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN`.
  - If you choose the NAS, confirm it has `gh`, `curl` and `jq` and can run `actions/checkout` and `create-github-app-token`.
  - This checkout has no git remote, so I cannot see your repository settings.
- **P7. Proof and cutover.**
  - Run a test PR against current main to show the old path. The test PR's own run shows the new path.
  - Show `ai-review` as success for a clean change and failure for a change with a blocking issue.
  - After merge, test `/rereview`. `issue_comment` events run the workflow file from the default branch, so this test cannot happen on the PR.
  - Keep the period when both the desktop and the cloud run reviews short.
  - Then stop the desktop runner and remove its reviewer sign-in.

- **P8. Guard the shared sign-in refresh.** You can serialize reviews or add a lock. A workflow `concurrency:` group cancels queued runs. Each cancelled run leaves `ai-review` "cancelled", which blocks merge.

# Plan: move the PR reviews from the desktop runner to the cloud routine

A fresh verifier agent checked my reading of the repo and this plan. It confirmed all eight facts below and flagged one gap and one scope problem. I fixed both in this plan. Nothing has been edited. The repo has no git remote, so nobody has checked the live GitHub state yet: runners, secrets, variables and branch protection.

## Facts the plan rests on
- Both workflows run on `[self-hosted, desktop]` and call `scripts/start_review.sh`. That script runs the reviewer CLI on the desktop (`pr-review.yml:8`, `rerun-review.yml:9`, `start_review.sh:4-8`).

- The routine starts on a POST to `vars.CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL`, with `secrets.CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN` as the bearer token. The JSON body holds `pull_request`, `model` and `effort`. The call blocks for up to 30 minutes and returns 200 (pass), 422 (blocking findings) or anything else (failure). The routine posts its own comments (`docs/cloud-routine.md:5-7`).
- The cloud proxy refuses check-run writes, so the workflow must keep ownership of the `ai-review` check (`notes/findings.md:3`). Branch protection requires that check (`notes/findings.md:5`, `check_run.sh:9-12`).
- The App private key has only been used from the desktop (`notes/findings.md:4`).

## Steps

1. **Check before building.** Run `gh variable list` and `gh secret list` to confirm the routine's URL variable and token secret exist. Add a `workflow_dispatch` job on `[self-hosted, nas]` that mints the App token and confirms `gh`, `curl` and Node are installed. This covers finding 4, and it needs no real pull request.
2. **Write the eval first.** Add a test script that starts a local stub server returning 200, 422, 500 or nothing, then checks the exit code of `start_review.sh` in each case. An environment variable sets the curl timeout, so the hang case finishes quickly. The test fails on today's script. A wrong twin that maps 422 to exit 0 must also fail it.
3. **Rewrite `scripts/start_review.sh`.** The script POSTs the PR number, `REVIEW_MODEL` and `REVIEW_EFFORT` with curl and a timeout of about 31 minutes. It maps 200 to exit 0, 422 to exit 1, and every other result to exit 2, curl timeouts and connection errors included. Each exit prints a clear message. The `--post-comments` flag goes away.
4. **Change both workflows.** Set `runs-on: [self-hosted, nas]` and `timeout-minutes: 35`. Pass `CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` and `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN` to the "Start reviewer" step. Keep the checkout, token, open-check and `if: always()` complete-check steps as they are. `ai-review` then passes only on a 200.
5. **Trial and cut over.** Open a trial PR. Confirm a pass, a 422, and a `/rereview`. Update the workflow and runner tables in `README.md` (lines 5-7, 16, 22, 23). The desktop runner stays registered until you approve its removal.

## Questions for you
- **NAS load.** The README describes the NAS as a place for "short jobs". Each review holds a NAS runner for up to 30 minutes, and while it waits it blocks other NAS jobs. Is that acceptable? The other choice is a GitHub-hosted runner.
- **Sign-in refresh race (new scope).** All cloud reviews share one sign-in. If two sessions refresh it at the same moment, one can be signed out (`notes/findings.md:2`). The move creates this risk. You have three options:
  - Do nothing. A failed review shows up as a failed check, and `/rereview` recovers it.
  - Add one global `concurrency` group so reviews run one at a time. If the NAS has only one runner, this already happens.
  - Build a lock and write-back system for the credential. This option costs the most.

## Existing issues the move does not fix (listed so you know about them)
- `check_run.sh` "complete" creates a second check run. The first `in_progress` run never closes.
- `complete-for-pr` looks up the head SHA again when it finishes. A push during the 30-minute wait can put the result on a different commit.
- Any commenter can type `/rereview`, and each one now costs a cloud run.

Most guides linked from `.claude/rules/index.md` are missing. Only `verified-work.md` exists. The `search-before-acting` skill and the `verifier` agent are also missing, so a general-purpose agent did the verification.

A fresh verifier agent checked the research and the first draft of this plan. Every research claim passed. ## What constrains the move

- **The cloud routine is a single blocking request.** You send a POST with `pull_request`, `model` and `effort`. The routine posts the review comments itself. It answers within 30 minutes: `200` means pass, `422` means blocking findings, and any other status means the routine failed (`docs/cloud-routine.md:5-7`).
- **The check run must stay in GitHub Actions.** The cloud proxy refuses writes to the check-runs API (`notes/findings.md:3`). The Actions job keeps the App token and the `scripts/check_run.sh` calls.
- **Every failure must block the merge.** Branch protection requires `ai-review` to pass (`notes/findings.md:5`). A non-zero exit fails the job, and the `always()` step then reports the failure as the conclusion (`pr-review.yml:25-27`).
- **The App key will be used on a new machine.** Until now it has only been used from the desktop (`notes/findings.md:4`).
- **Reviews run one at a time today.** The desktop is a single runner. Parallel reviews worked in the trial, but two sessions that refresh the shared sign-in at the same moment can sign one out. That refresh happens about every 10 days (`notes/findings.md:1-2`).

## Steps

1. **Write the eval first.** Add a test that starts a local stub HTTP server and runs the new script against these answers:
   - `200` must exit 0.
   - `422` must exit 1.
   - `500`, a failed connection and a hang must each exit 2.

   The test must fail before the script exists. It must also fail against a broken copy that maps `422` to 0, and fail again when the change is undone.
2. **Add `scripts/start_cloud_review.sh`.** It sends a POST to `$CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` with the bearer token `$CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN`. The body is `{pull_request, model: $REVIEW_MODEL, effort: $REVIEW_EFFORT}`. The curl time limit is 1860 s, and an environment variable can override it so the hang test runs fast. It maps the status codes to the exit codes from step 1.
3. **Change both workflows.** In `pr-review.yml` and `rerun-review.yml`:
   - Set `runs-on` to the runner you pick in decision A below.
   - Point the "Start reviewer" step at the new script. Pass `vars.CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL`, `secrets.CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN`, `vars.REVIEW_MODEL` and `vars.REVIEW_EFFORT`.

Compare the `ai-review` conclusion and the posted comments, and quote both under "Proof in practice". `/rereview` runs the workflow from the default branch, so you can test it only after the merge.
5. **Retire the desktop path after step 4 passes.**
   - Remove `scripts/start_review.sh` with `git rm`.

- **C. Check run fix (optional, not needed for the move).** `check_run.sh` creates a second check run on complete. It does not update the one it opened (`scripts/check_run.sh:9-12`). The move works without fixing this.

+#!/bin/bash
+# Runs scripts/start_review.sh against a fake curl and checks the exit code for each routine status.
+set -uo pipefail
+repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -rf -- "$work"' EXIT
+
+cat >"$work/curl" <<'EOF'
+#!/bin/bash
+# Fake curl: records stdin and args, writes a body to --output, prints FAKE_STATUS.
+cat >"$FAKE_DIR/stdin"
+printf '%s\n' "$@" >"$FAKE_DIR/args"
+while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
+  case "$1" in --output) echo '{"ok":true}' >"$2"; shift ;; esac
+  shift
+done
+printf '%s' "$FAKE_STATUS"
+EOF
+chmod +x "$work/curl"
+
+export PATH="$work:$PATH" FAKE_DIR="$work"
+export CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL=https://routine.example/fire CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=secret-token
+export REVIEW_MODEL=model-x REVIEW_EFFORT=high
+
+failures=0
+check() {
+  if [ "$2" = "$3" ]; then echo "PASS $1"; else echo "FAIL $1: expected $2, got $3"; failures=$((failures + 1)); fi
+}
+
+for case in "200 0" "422 1" "500 2" "000 2"; do
+  set -- $case
+  FAKE_STATUS=$1 "$repo/scripts/start_review.sh" 42 >/dev/null 2>&1
+  check "HTTP $1 exits $2" "$2" "$?"
+done
+
+FAKE_STATUS=200 "$repo/scripts/start_review.sh" 42 >/dev/null 2>&1
+check "body" '{"pull_request":42,"model":"model-x","effort":"high"}' "$(grep -A1 -x -- --data "$work/args" | tail -n1)"
+check "token sent on stdin" 'header = "Authorization: Bearer secret-token"' "$(cat "$work/stdin")"
+check "token absent from args" 0 "$(grep -c secret-token "$work/args")"
+check "posts to CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL" "$CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL" "$(tail -n1 "$work/args")"
+
+CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN='bad"token' FAKE_STATUS=200 "$repo/scripts/start_review.sh" 42 >/dev/null 2>&1
+check "token with a quote rejected" 2 "$?"
+
+FAKE_STATUS=200 "$repo/scripts/start_review.sh" '42,"x":1' >/dev/null 2>&1
+check "non-numeric pull request rejected" 2 "$?"
+
+exit "$failures"

+#!/bin/bash
+set -euo pipefail
+pull_request_number=$1
+if ! [[ "$pull_request_number" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
+  echo "pull request number must be numeric: $pull_request_number" >&2

+body=$(jq -n \
+  --argjson pull_request "$pull_request_number" \
+  --arg model "${REVIEW_MODEL:?}" \
+  --arg effort "${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}" \
+  '{pull_request: $pull_request, model: $model, effort: $effort}')

+trap 'rm -f "$response"' EXIT

+  -X POST "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL:?}" \
+  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}" \
+  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+  --data "$body")
+cat "$response"
+echo

+  200) echo "review passed" ;;
+  422) echo "reviewer reported blocking findings" >&2; exit 1 ;;
+  *) echo "cloud routine failed with HTTP $status" >&2; exit 1 ;;
+esac

+#!/bin/bash
+# Runs scripts/cloud_review.sh against a local stub of the cloud routine.
+set -uo pipefail
+root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'kill "$server" 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
+
+cat > "$work/stub.py" <<'EOF'
+import http.server, json, sys
+class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"])))
+        ok = (self.headers.get("Authorization") == "Bearer t0ken"
+              and body == {"pull_request": 42, "model": "m", "effort": body["effort"]})
+        code = int(body["effort"]) if ok else 400
+        self.send_response(code)
+        self.end_headers()
+        self.wfile.write(b"stub says %d" % code)
+    def log_message(self, *a): pass
+s = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), H)
+print(s.server_port, flush=True)
+s.serve_forever()
+EOF
+python3 "$work/stub.py" > "$work/port" &
+server=$!
+for _ in $(seq 50); do [ -s "$work/port" ] && break; sleep 0.1; done
+port=$(cat "$work/port")
+
+failures=0
+expect() {
+  local want=$1 effort=$2 url=$3
+  REVIEW_MODEL=m REVIEW_EFFORT=$effort CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=t0ken CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL=$url \
+    "$root/scripts/cloud_review.sh" 42 > /dev/null 2>&1
+  local got=$?
+  if [ "$got" -eq "$want" ]; then echo "ok   effort=$effort exit=$got"
+  else echo "FAIL effort=$effort want=$want got=$got"; failures=$((failures + 1)); fi
+}
+expect 0 200 "http://127.0.0.1:$port/"
+expect 1 422 "http://127.0.0.1:$port/"
+expect 1 500 "http://127.0.0.1:$port/"
+expect 1 200 "http://127.0.0.1:1/"
+exit "$failures"

+  local got=$?
+  if [ "$got" -eq "$want" ]; then echo "ok   $name"; else echo "FAIL $name: exit $got, want $want"; failures=$((failures + 1)); fi

+#!/bin/bash
+# Runs scripts/cloud_review.sh against a local mock of the cloud routine.
+# The mock answers with the status code named in the request path.
+set -uo pipefail
+cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
+log=$(mktemp)
+portfile=$(mktemp)
+python3 -I - "$portfile" "$log" <<'EOF' &
+import http.server, json, sys
+portfile, log = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
+class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"]))
+        with open(log, "a") as f:
+            f.write(json.dumps({"auth": self.headers["Authorization"], "body": json.loads(body)}) + "\n")
+        self.send_response(int(self.path.strip("/")))
+        self.end_headers()
+    def log_message(self, *a):
+        pass
+server = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), H)
+open(portfile, "w").write(str(server.server_port))
+server.serve_forever()
+EOF
+server=$!
+trap 'kill $server; wait $server 2>/dev/null; rm -f "$log" "$portfile"' EXIT
+for _ in $(seq 50); do [ -s "$portfile" ] && break; sleep 0.1; done
+port=$(cat "$portfile")
+
+fails=0
+expect() {
+  local code=$1 want=$2
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$port/$code" CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=t0k \
+    REVIEW_MODEL=m1 REVIEW_EFFORT=high scripts/cloud_review.sh 42 >/dev/null 2>&1
+  local got=$?

+  else echo "FAIL HTTP $code -> exit $got, want $want"; fails=1; fi
+}
+expect 200 0
+expect 422 1
+expect 500 1
+CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:1/" CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=t REVIEW_MODEL=m REVIEW_EFFORT=e \
+  scripts/cloud_review.sh 42 >/dev/null 2>&1 \
+  && { echo "FAIL unreachable routine -> exit 0, want 1"; fails=1; } \
+  || echo "ok   unreachable routine -> exit 1"
+
+want='{"auth": "Bearer t0k", "body": {"pull_request": 42, "model": "m1", "effort": "high"}}'

+else echo "FAIL request was: $(head -n1 "$log")"; fails=1; fi

+#!/bin/bash
+# Fires the cloud routine and waits for the review to finish.
+# Exit 0: review passed. Exit 1: blocking findings. Exit 2: the routine failed.
+set -euo pipefail
+pull_request_number=$1
+body=$(jq -n \
+  --argjson pull_request "$pull_request_number" \
+  --arg model "${REVIEW_MODEL:?}" \
+  --arg effort "${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}" \
+  '{pull_request: $pull_request, model: $model, effort: $effort}')
+response=$(mktemp)
+trap 'rm -f "$response"' EXIT
+status=$(curl -sS --max-time 1860 -o "$response" -w '%{http_code}' \
+  -X POST "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL:?}" \
+  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}" \
+  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+  --data "$body") || status=000
+case "$status" in
+  200) echo "Review passed." ;;
+  422) echo "Reviewer reported blocking findings." >&2; exit 1 ;;
+  *) echo "Cloud routine failed with HTTP $status:" >&2; cat "$response" >&2; exit 2 ;;
+esac

+#!/bin/bash
+# Runs scripts/start_cloud_review.sh against a local stub of the cloud routine
+# and checks the exit code and request body for each routine status.
+set -euo pipefail
+here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'kill "$stub_pid" 2>/dev/null || true; rm -r "$work"' EXIT
+
+cat > "$work/stub.py" <<'EOF'
+import http.server, json, sys
+work = sys.argv[1]
+class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"]))
+        with open(f"{work}/last_request", "w") as f:
+            json.dump({"auth": self.headers.get("Authorization"), "body": json.loads(body)}, f)
+        status = int(open(f"{work}/next_status").read())
+        self.send_response(status)
+        self.end_headers()
+        self.wfile.write(b"stub body")
+    def log_message(self, *a): pass
+s = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), H)
+open(f"{work}/port", "w").write(str(s.server_address[1]))
+s.serve_forever()
+EOF
+python3 -I "$work/stub.py" "$work" &
+stub_pid=$!
+for _ in $(seq 50); do [ -s "$work/port" ] && break; sleep 0.1; done
+
+export CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$(cat "$work/port")/fire"
+export CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=test-token
+export REVIEW_MODEL='model "with" quotes'
+export REVIEW_EFFORT=high
+export NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1 no_proxy=127.0.0.1
+
+failures=0

+  local status=$1 want=$2 got=0
+  echo "$status" > "$work/next_status"
+  "$here/start_cloud_review.sh" 42 > /dev/null 2>&1 || got=$?
+  if [ "$got" = "$want" ]; then echo "ok   status $status -> exit $got"
+  else echo "FAIL status $status -> exit $got, want $want"; failures=$((failures + 1)); fi
+}
+expect 200 0
+expect 422 1
+expect 500 2
+expect 401 2
+
+want='{"auth":"Bearer test-token","body":{"pull_request":42,"model":"model \"with\" quotes","effort":"high"}}'
+got=$(jq -cS . "$work/last_request")
+if [ "$got" = "$(jq -cS . <<< "$want")" ]; then echo "ok   request body"
+else echo "FAIL request body: $got"; failures=$((failures + 1)); fi
+
+[ "$failures" = 0 ]

+#!/bin/bash
+# Fires the cloud routine and waits for the review. See docs/cloud-routine.md.
+# Exit 0: review passed. Exit 1: blocking findings. Exit 2: the routine failed.
+set -euo pipefail
+pull_request_number=$1
+body=$(jq -n \
+  --argjson pull_request "$pull_request_number" \
+  --arg model "${REVIEW_MODEL:?}" \
+  --arg effort "${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}" \
+  '{pull_request: $pull_request, model: $model, effort: $effort}')

+  -X POST "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL:?}" \
+  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}" \
+  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+  -d "$body") || status=000
+case "$status" in
+  200) echo "Review passed" ;;
+  422) echo "Reviewer reported blocking findings" >&2; exit 1 ;;

+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'kill "$stub_pid" 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
+

+import http.server, json, sys
+out = sys.argv[1]
+class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):

+EOF

+#!/bin/bash
+# Fires the cloud review routine and waits for its result. See docs/cloud-routine.md.
+# Exit 0: review passed. Exit 1: blocking findings. Exit 3: the routine failed.
+set -euo pipefail
+pull_request_number=$1
+[[ "$pull_request_number" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || { echo "bad pull request number: $pull_request_number" >&2; exit 2; }
+: "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL:?}" "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}"

+  --argjson pull_request "$pull_request_number" \
+  --arg model "${REVIEW_MODEL:?}" \
+  --arg effort "${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}" \
+  '{pull_request: $pull_request, model: $model, effort: $effort}')
+# The routine holds the request open for up to 30 minutes.

+  -X POST \
+  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}" \
+  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+  -d "$body" \
+  "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL:?}") || { echo "cloud routine request failed" >&2; exit 3; }
+case "$status" in
+  200) echo "review passed" ;;
+  422) echo "reviewer reported blocking findings" >&2; exit 1 ;;
+  *) echo "cloud routine failed with HTTP $status" >&2; exit 3 ;;
+esac

+#!/bin/bash
+# Runs scripts/cloud_review.sh against a local stub of the cloud routine.
+# Usage: scripts/test_cloud_review.sh
+set -uo pipefail
+here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'kill "$stub_pid" 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
+
+cat > "$work/stub.py" <<'EOF'
+import http.server, json, sys
+status_file, log_file = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
+class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"]))
+        with open(log_file, "w") as f:
+            json.dump({"auth": self.headers["Authorization"], "body": json.loads(body)}, f)
+        self.send_response(int(open(status_file).read()))
+        self.end_headers()
+    def log_message(self, *args):
+        pass
+server = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
+print(server.server_port, flush=True)
+server.serve_forever()
+EOF
+
+python3 -I "$work/stub.py" "$work/status" "$work/request.json" > "$work/port" &
+stub_pid=$!
+for _ in $(seq 50); do [ -s "$work/port" ] && break; sleep 0.1; done
+port=$(cat "$work/port")
+
+failures=0
+check() {
+  local status=$1 want_exit=$2
+  echo "$status" > "$work/status"
+  rm -f "$work/request.json"
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$port/fire" CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=secret-token \
+    REVIEW_MODEL=model-x REVIEW_EFFORT=high \
+    "$here/cloud_review.sh" 42 > "$work/out" 2>&1
+  local got_exit=$?
+  local want_request='{"auth":"Bearer secret-token","body":{"pull_request":42,"model":"model-x","effort":"high"}}'
+  local got_request
+  got_request=$(jq -c . "$work/request.json" 2>/dev/null)
+  if [ "$got_exit" = "$want_exit" ] && [ "$got_request" = "$want_request" ]; then
+    echo "PASS  HTTP $status -> exit $got_exit"
+  else
+    echo "FAIL  HTTP $status -> exit $got_exit (want $want_exit), request $got_request"
+    sed 's/^/      /' "$work/out"
+    failures=$((failures + 1))
+  fi
+}
+
+check 200 0
+check 422 1
+check 500 3
+[ "$failures" = 0 ] && echo "all passed"
+exit "$failures"

+#!/bin/bash
+# Runs scripts/start_review.sh against a stub curl and checks the exit code
+# for each status the cloud routine can return.
+set -uo pipefail
+root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'find "$work" -delete' EXIT
+
+cat > "$work/curl" <<'EOF'
+#!/bin/bash
+# Stub: record the request, then print the status code in STUB_STATUS.
+cat > "$STUB_DIR/config"
+printf '%s\n' "$@" > "$STUB_DIR/args"
+[ "$STUB_STATUS" = "000" ] && { printf '000'; exit 7; }
+printf '%s' "$STUB_STATUS"
+EOF
+chmod +x "$work/curl"
+
+fail=0
+run() {
+  local status=$1 want=$2
+  STUB_DIR=$work STUB_STATUS=$status PATH="$work:$PATH" \
+    CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL=https://routine.example/fire CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=${TOKEN:-tok123} \
+    REVIEW_MODEL=model-x REVIEW_EFFORT=high \
+    "$root/scripts/start_review.sh" 42 </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
+  local got=$?
+  if [ "$got" = "$want" ]; then
+    echo "PASS status=$status exit=$got"
+  else
+    echo "FAIL status=$status exit=$got want=$want"; fail=1
+  fi
+}
+
+run 200 0
+run 422 1
+run 500 1
+run 401 1
+run 000 1
+
+# The request must carry the PR, model and effort, and the token must stay off the command line.
+run 200 0 >/dev/null
+body=$(grep -A1 -- '--data' "$work/args" | tail -1)
+if [ "$(jq -c . <<<"$body")" = '{"pull_request":42,"model":"model-x","effort":"high"}' ]; then
+  echo "PASS body"
+else
+  echo "FAIL body: $body"; fail=1
+fi
+if [ ! -s "$work/args" ] || grep -q tok123 "$work/args"; then echo "FAIL token on command line"; fail=1; else echo "PASS token off command line"; fi
+if grep -q 'Bearer tok123' "$work/config"; then echo "PASS token in header"; else echo "FAIL token missing from header"; fail=1; fi
+grep -qx https://routine.example/fire "$work/args" && echo "PASS url" || { echo "FAIL url"; fail=1; }
+
+# A token with a quote or backslash must reach the header unchanged.
+TOKEN='a"b\c' run 200 0 >/dev/null
+if grep -qF 'Bearer a\"b\\c' "$work/config"; then echo "PASS token escaped"; else echo "FAIL token escaped: $(cat "$work/config")"; fail=1; fi
+
+exit $fail

+#!/bin/bash
+# Runs scripts/start_review.sh against a local mock of the cloud routine.
+set -uo pipefail
+repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'kill "$server" 2>/dev/null; rm -r "$work"' EXIT
+
+cat > "$work/mock.py" <<'EOF'
+import http.server, sys
+out = sys.argv[1]
+class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"]))
+        with open(out, "w") as f:
+            f.write(self.headers["Authorization"] + "\n" + body.decode())
+        self.send_response(int(self.path.strip("/")))
+        self.end_headers()
+    def log_message(self, *a):
+        pass
+s = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), H)
+print(s.server_port, flush=True)
+s.serve_forever()
+EOF
+coproc MOCK { python3 -u "$work/mock.py" "$work/request"; }
+server=$MOCK_PID
+read -r port <&"${MOCK[0]}"
+
+fail=0
+run() {  # expected_exit http_status
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$port/$2" CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=tok \
+    REVIEW_MODEL=model-from-vars REVIEW_EFFORT=high \

+  got=$?
+  if [ "$got" -ne "$1" ]; then echo "FAIL: HTTP $2 gave exit $got, want $1"; fail=1; else echo "ok: HTTP $2 -> exit $got"; fi

+run 0 200
+want='{"pull_request":42,"model":"model-from-vars","effort":"high"}'

+trap 'kill "$stub_pid" 2>/dev/null || true; rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
+

+import http.server, json, sys
+work = sys.argv[1]
+class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"]))
+        with open(f"{work}/request.json", "wb") as f:
+            f.write(body)
+        with open(f"{work}/auth", "w") as f:

+        status = int(open(f"{work}/status").read())
+        self.send_response(status)
+        self.end_headers()
+        self.wfile.write(b"stub response")
+    def log_message(self, *args):
+        pass
+server = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
+open(f"{work}/port", "w").write(str(server.server_port))
+server.serve_forever()
+EOF

+stub_pid=$!
+for _ in $(seq 50); do [ -s "$work/port" ] && break; sleep 0.1; done

+export CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=test-token
+export REVIEW_MODEL=test-model
+export REVIEW_EFFORT=test-effort

+    failures=$((failures + 1))
+  fi
+}
+expect 200 0
+expect 422 1
+expect 500 1
+
+want='{"effort":"test-effort","model":"test-model","pull_request":42}'

+work=$(mktemp -d)

+import http.server, json, sys
+out = sys.argv[1]
+class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"]))
+        with open(out, "w") as f:
+            json.dump({"path": self.path, "auth": self.headers["Authorization"],
+                       "body": json.loads(body)}, f)
+        self.send_response(int(self.path.strip("/")))
+        self.end_headers()
+    def log_message(self, *a): pass
+s = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), H)
+print(s.server_port, flush=True)
+s.serve_forever()
+EOF
+python3 -I "$work/stub.py" "$work/request.json" > "$work/port" &
+server_pid=$!
+for _ in $(seq 50); do [ -s "$work/port" ] && break; sleep 0.1; done

meta.prior_reply:
# Plan: move PR reviews from the desktop runner to the cloud routine

A separate verifier agent checked this plan against the repo files. It found one wrong piece, a shared concurrency group, and I removed it. I have edited no files.

## What stays the same, and why

- **The workflow keeps the check run.** The cloud session's proxy refuses writes to the check-runs API (`notes/findings.md:3`). Branch protection requires `ai-review` (`notes/findings.md:5`). So the GitHub job still mints the App token, opens `ai-review`, and completes it with `job.status`. `scripts/check_run.sh` does not change.
- **The routine posts the review comments** (`docs/cloud-routine.md:6`). The job only fires the routine and maps its HTTP status to a pass or a fail.

## In-scope changes

1. **Runner.** In `.github/workflows/pr-review.yml:8` and `.github/workflows/rerun-review.yml:9`, change `runs-on` from `[self-hosted, desktop]` to the new runner. I recommend `[self-hosted, nas]`, because the README names it for HTTP calls (`README.md:23`). See question 1.
2. **`scripts/start_review.sh`.** Replace the `reviewer exec review` call with one `curl` POST:
   - The URL is `CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL`, with `Authorization: Bearer $CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN`.
   - The body holds `pull_request`, `model` and `effort`, built with `jq`. The script never prints the token.
   - `--max-time` is a little over 30 minutes (`docs/cloud-routine.md:7`).
   - Status 200 exits 0. Status 422 exits 1. Any other status or a timeout also exits 1.
3. **Workflow env.** The step keeps `REVIEW_MODEL` and `REVIEW_EFFORT`, and adds `CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` from `vars` and `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN` from `secrets`.
4. **Job timeout.** Set `timeout-minutes: 40` on both jobs. The GitHub default is 360 minutes. A timeout gives `cancelled`, which still fails the required check.
5. **README.** Update the description at `README.md:5-7`, the scripts line at `:16`, and the runner table at `:22-23`. Link to `docs/cloud-routine.md`.

## Checks before I build

- Run `gh variable list` and `gh secret list` to confirm that `CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` and `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN` exist.
- Confirm that the chosen runner has `gh`, `curl`, `jq`, and the Node that `actions/checkout` and `create-github-app-token` need.

## Eval and proof

- **Local eval.** A re-runnable script starts a stub HTTP server that returns 200, 422, 500, or a slow reply. It runs `start_review.sh` against each case and checks the exit code.
  - The eval must fail against the current script.
  - A wrong twin must fail it, for example a script that exits 0 on 422.
  - It must fail again after the change is undone.
- **Live test.** On a test PR, fire both workflows: a push and a `/rereview` comment. Confirm the `ai-review` conclusion on the head SHA, and confirm that the routine posted comments.
- A fresh verifier checks the fix. Before any PR, I load `pr-lifecycle` and quote runs with and without the change under "Proof in practice".

## Not in this plan (new scope, ask first)

- **Coordinating sign-in refreshes inside the routine.** One shared reviewer sign-in refreshes about every 10 days. Two refreshes at the same moment can sign one session out (`notes/findings.md:2`). That risk remains after the move. Running two reviews at once was fine in the trials (`notes/findings.md:1`).
- **A workflow `concurrency` group.** I dropped it. GitHub cancels any queued run when a newer one joins the group. A PR whose run was cancelled before its check opened would get no `ai-review` check, and its merge would stay blocked.
- **Taking the desktop runner out of service.** It stays registered.

## Accepted behavior

If `curl` times out, the check fails. The routine can still post its comments afterwards.

## Questions for you

1. **Runner choice.** The NAS is meant for "short jobs" (`README.md:23`), and this job can wait up to 30 minutes. The App private key has only ever been used from the desktop (`notes/findings.md:4`). Is the NAS acceptable for both? If not, a GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` runner can do the same job.
2. **Sign-in refresh.** Do you want the refresh coordination planned as a separate piece of work?

+#!/bin/bash
+# Runs scripts/start_review.sh (or the script given as $1) against a stub
+# cloud routine and checks the exit code for each routine status.
+set -uo pipefail
+here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
+script=${1:-$here/../scripts/start_review.sh}
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'kill "$stub" 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
+failures=0
+
+run_case() {
+  local name=$1 status=$2 delay=$3 max_time=$4 want=$5
+  local port=$((20000 + RANDOM % 20000))
+  : > "$work/log"
+  python3 "$here/stub_routine.py" "$port" "$status" "$delay" "$work/log" &
+  stub=$!
+  for _ in $(seq 50); do
+    curl -s -o /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:$port" && break
+    sleep 0.1
+  done
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$port/fire" \
+    CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=test-token \
+    CLOUD_ROUTINE_MAX_TIME="$max_time" \
+    REVIEW_MODEL=test-model \
+    REVIEW_EFFORT=high \
+    PATH="$work/bin:$PATH" \
+    bash "$script" 42 > "$work/out" 2>&1
+  local got=$?
+  kill "$stub" 2>/dev/null
+  wait "$stub" 2>/dev/null
+  local ok=1
+  [ "$got" = "$want" ] || ok=0
+  if ! jq -e 'select(.auth == "Bearer test-token") | .body | fromjson
+      | select(.pull_request == 42 and .model == "test-model" and .effort == "high")' \
+      "$work/log" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
+    ok=0
+  fi
+  if grep -q test-token "$work/out"; then
+    ok=0
+  fi

+    echo "PASS $name (exit $got)"
+  else
+    echo "FAIL $name (exit $got, want $want; request: $(cat "$work/log"))"
+    failures=$((failures + 1))
+  fi

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Stub cloud routine for tests/start_review_test.sh.
+
+Usage: stub_routine.py PORT STATUS DELAY_SECONDS LOG_FILE
+Answers every POST with STATUS after DELAY_SECONDS and appends the
+Authorization header and request body to LOG_FILE as one JSON line.
+"""
+import json
+import sys
+import time
+from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer
+
+port, status, delay, log_file = int(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2]), float(sys.argv[3]), sys.argv[4]
+
+
+class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))).decode()
+        with open(log_file, "a") as f:
+            f.write(json.dumps({"auth": self.headers.get("Authorization"), "body": body}) + "\n")
+        time.sleep(delay)
+        self.send_response(status)
+        self.end_headers()
+        self.wfile.write(b"{}")
+
+    def log_message(self, *args):
+        pass
+
